issues.description: setuptools<82 cap leaks from CI workaround into core/setup.py runtime install_requires.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flag this as the central scope violation. The mmcv pkg_resources breakage is a build-time CI problem, but pinning setuptools<82 in core/setup.py forces every downstream consumer of the hyperopt extra to inherit the ceiling. The cap belongs in CI scripts (env_setup.sh, setup_mmcv.sh) or pyproject build-system requires, not runtime contract.

issues.description: setuptools<82 constraint duplicated across three sites with no shared spec or revert criteria.
issues.detail: The same pin appears in env_setup.sh, setup_mmcv.sh, and core/setup.py with inconsistent FIXME coverage and no single source of truth. There is no stated postcondition for lifting the cap (e.g., "once mmcv#3325 ships a wheel that doesn't import pkg_resources") and no owner. When upstream resolves, one of three sites will be missed.

issues.description: mmdet silently bumped from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 with no rationale in the diff.
issues.detail: PR is titled as a mmengine fix but quietly rides a minor version bump of mmdet. No justification for why 3.3.0 is required vs retaining 3.2.0, no test evidence. Should either be split into a separate patch or annotated with the compatibility reason tying it to mmengine 0.10.7 / mmcv 2.1.0.

issues.description: --no-build-isolation silently widens mmcv's build contract to ambient environment state.
issues.detail: Disabling PEP 517 isolation means mmcv's build now depends on whatever setuptools, wheel, and torch the ambient interpreter provides. This works only because setuptools<82 is pre-installed two lines earlier and torch is assumed present. The implicit ordering invariant is unstated and brittle to step reordering across CI runners.

issues.description: mmengine git SHA replaced by 0.10.7 pin without restating the torch-2.5 compatibility invariant.
issues.detail: The prior pinned SHA existed specifically to carry a torch 2.5 fix. Substituting mmengine==0.10.7 drops that explicit contract; a one-line note confirming the upstream fix landed in 0.10.7 would make the substitution auditable. Same applies to the mim-install to raw-pip switch, which loses mim's torch/CUDA wheel matching.

synthesis.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The patch is a reasonable CI unblock — capping setuptools<82 to dodge mmcv's pkg_resources breakage and replacing a mmengine git SHA with a PyPI pin — but it has scope and hygiene problems. The dominant issue, flagged unanimously, is that the setuptools cap leaks from CI scripts into core/setup.py runtime install_requires, pushing a build-time workaround onto every downstream user. The constraint is duplicated across three sites with no shared spec, no consistent FIXME, and no revert criteria, guaranteeing drift when upstream resolves. A silent mmdet 3.2.0->3.3.0 bump and an unannotated switch to --no-build-isolation ride along without justification. Fix the scope leak, consolidate the pin with a clear revert condition, and either justify or split the version bumps.
